subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub build the shared Weekly/Monthly/All time temporal popularity foundation across publishers, skills, and plugins before adding the requested browse tabs?
rationale: Current main has partial seven-day trending for skills/plugins but lacks publisher temporal rollups and monthly/snapshot-pinned period semantics, so implementation depends on maintainer choices about scope, scoring, and attribution.

options.title: Build shared temporal foundation first
options.body: Use the RFC sequence: finish package/publisher daily rollups, add weekly/monthly snapshot leaderboards, then add period tabs backed by the same contract across all surfaces.

options.title: Narrow to existing Trending
options.body: Keep the current seven-day Trending affordance for skills/plugins and explicitly defer publisher and monthly period popularity until a later product cycle.

options.title: Defer the RFC
options.body: Leave the current all-time/recommended browse surfaces unchanged and close or pause period popularity until discovery becomes a higher priority.

recommendation.title: Build shared temporal foundation first
recommendation.body: Use the RFC sequence: finish package/publisher daily rollups, add weekly/monthly snapshot leaderboards, then add period tabs backed by the same contract across all surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the RFC and introduced the publisher discovery surface that drives the hardest remaining product decision.
